English.Char_Desc_80: Reads print and handwriting in photos of pages and saves editable Word files.
English.Char_Desc_250: Pick a folder of photos of printed or handwritten pages. The text in each photo is read (OCR) and saved as an editable Word file, laid out roughly where it sat on the page: one Word file per photo, or all photos in one file, a page each.

English.Char_Desc_2000:
Photos to Word turns photos and scans of pages, printed or handwritten, into Word (.docx) files you can edit. Click One Word file for each photo or All photos in one Word file, then pick the folder. The text in each picture is read by RapidOCR, a free reader that works on this computer (nothing is uploaded), and placed on the page roughly where it appears in the photo, with columns lined up and font sizes scaled. A page photographed sideways or upside down is turned the right way up, and a slightly tilted photo is straightened. Works with JPG, PNG, TIFF (16-bit scans too), BMP, GIF and WebP pictures. Word files you corrected earlier are only replaced if you say so. Microsoft Word is not needed to make the files, only to open them. Everything it needs is included.
Before you install: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. The installer is not code-signed (a signing certificate is a paid yearly service), so Windows may show a blue "Windows protected your PC" box: click More info, then Run anyway. A few antivirus programs wrongly flag new unsigned programs; you can check the download against the SHA-256 fingerprint on its release page. No administrator password is needed.

Permissions.Distribution_Permissions: Photos to Word is free to use and share. Download sites may list it and offer the unchanged Setup.exe, or link to the download page.
Permissions.EULA: Photos to Word is free and comes with no warranty. Use it at your own risk. The free parts it is built from keep their own licenses, listed in the licenses folder it installs.
